title: Disclosure of Personal Data when Government Addresses Public Complaints
what_it_is: Disclosure of Personal Data when Government Addresses Public Complaints

sections.label: Agencies correcting inaccuracies for public trust
sections.summary: Government agencies must correct inaccuracies and provide an accurate picture to maintain public trust and serve citizens effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Government agencies have to do so to correct inaccuracies and provide an accurate picture of what occurred so as to maintain public trust and to serve all citizens effectively.

sections.label: Personal data disclosure in clarifications
sections.summary: Personal data is disclosed only if clarifications would otherwise be disputable or unclear, though identity may be disclosed to remove ambiguity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: First, personal data is disclosed only if the agency's clarifications would be disputable or insufficiently clear, without the disclosure of such personal data.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: These considerations serve to safeguard personal data from unnecessary public disclosure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: However, on occasion, it will be necessary to disclose the identity of the person involved in the case, even when the publicised complaint itself has been anonymised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This is to remove any ambiguity in the Government’s statement of the facts and settle any doubts over the matter conclusively in the minds of the public.

sections.label: Protocol for agreed agency statements
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government will consider a protocol where agencies first seek the person's agreement to a clarifying statement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider a protocol where agencies first try to get the person concerned to agree to a statement put out by the agency that clarifies matters?

sections.label: Not constraining agency responses
sections.summary: It would be inappropriate to constrain agencies' responses to an inaccurate or outright false public statement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The second thing is that, as a result of this, it would be inappropriate for us to constrain the agencies' response to an inaccurate or outright false public statement.

sections.label: Public replies to disinformation complaints
sections.summary: Agencies should reply in public and disclose information when public disinformation misrepresents Government policies, to set the record straight.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The bottom line is that should a complaint of this nature occur in public, associated with disinformation and which impacts the way in which the Government processes Government policies that serve citizens are being misrepresented, we should expect agencies to reply in public and disclose information so that we can set the record straight and make sure that Singapore and Singaporeans are well informed.

sections.label: Citizens seeking redress unaffected
sections.summary: Nothing in the PDPA or the answer prevents or discourages a citizen from seeking redress from a complaint.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: PDPA notwithstanding and my answer notwithstanding, none of this prevents or is meant to discourage a citizen from seeking redress from a complaint.
